This report supersedes report.md for the validation status. The original report remains preserved. Candidate only; no mainline tool replacement, integration, formal review pass, production speed claim, or product delivery.

- results.json contains raw per-case output. Passed 19; failed 0; unsupported 1; blocked 0.
- Real filesystem checks passed: literal duplicates, parent/child and file/parent overlap, hardlink identity, '..' path, missing file, disappearance between calls and during traversal (both raised FileNotFoundError), growth and replacement between calls, symlink reparse refusal, and propagated scan error. Actual same-domain Session check rejected an oversized additional request and mocked insufficient disk free space; same-process nested entry refused while this Session held the lock.
- Current volume refused creating distinct Case and case directories. The component branch passed only with two synthetic distinct identities; real case-sensitive filesystem behavior remains unverified. A Windows junction was not separately tested. Cross-process lock contention was not repeated here.
- Identical benchmark input: 32 references to two logical files, 8 bytes both versions. Root visits 32 versus 1; os.scandir calls 40 versus 2. Raw timings are in results.json.

- Every supplied root, including one covered by a parent, goes through regular_tree. The selected tree is still enumerated by files_under and checks each node for symlink/reparse or irregular type. Reparse and I/O errors remain fail closed.
- Each size() call builds its own coverage set and measures actual st_size. No cross-call byte or directory cache is used. The existing (st_dev, st_ino) set still counts hardlink aliases once. Case-sensitive Path.parts components are compared without case folding; unresolved '..' paths are scanned separately.
- Session shared lock, ledger validation, operation/retained budget, disk reserve and process runner remain unchanged. A running output is remeasured on each check; this small fixture does not prove behavior under a concurrently writing external process or atomic snapshot semantics.

## Intake and remaining verification

1. User chooses when to notify or receive. Mainline executor first confirms source SHA256, current bundle identity, branch and writer state, and checks whether any external writes or changed path semantics invalidate this patch. The bundle had a prior drift on two process documents; this candidate did not resolve or update it.
2. Before integration, repeat focused tests on a real case-sensitive filesystem and Windows junction, verify cross-process Session lock behavior, low-policy retained limit on an isolated fixture, and affected full storage/process runner regressions under the approved budget domain. Keep any failures and baseline identities.
3. Only after bytes agree on a fixed same-version input should mainline measure time and scan calls under a safe window. Do not run a full real-ledger stress loop, infer speed from root-count reduction, or treat this candidate as formal review or product acceptance.
